NOVELTY STATEMENT
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme via simple thresholding of condenser water delta-T (ΔT) against a static baseline, which fails under open cooling-tower variable-ambient conditions. Your departure: a dynamic "Effective Approach Temperature" indicator that normalizes the measured condenser ΔT against the simultaneous ambient wet-bulb temperature and chiller load (kW), creating a drift-detection signal isolated from environmental noise, triggering at a calculated pre-trip threshold.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: Condenser heat rejection (Q) = m_dot * cp * ΔT_cond. As tubes foul, thermal resistance (R_foul) increases, reducing the overall heat transfer coefficient (U). For a fixed load and cooling tower wet-bulb temperature (T_wb), the condenser leaving temperature (T_out) rises, and the "Approach" (T_out - T_wb) widens. The compressor head (high-side pressure ratio) is exponentially related to this approach.
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = tube-side fouling thermal resistance (R_foul); the mechanism moves it <down> (via scheduled automated chemical dosing triggered by the indicator); this <reduces> the condenser approach temperature differential and compressor power draw.
Magnitude verification: At 900 kW, a 1 °C increase in condenser approach typically costs ~3-5% compressor power (approx. 30-45 kW). The trip occurs at high-head; a 14-day lead time requires detecting a slow drift of ~0.5 °C/week in the normalized approach.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
MECHANISM CLASS: Dynamic Environmental Normalization with Automated Chemical Dosing

1. Data Feed 1: Condenser Water Inlet/Outlet Temperature (ALREADY-RECORDED: stated in constraint "existing condenser-water inlet/outlet temperature"). (a)
2. Data Feed 2: Condenser Water Flow (ALREADY-RECORDED: stated in constraint "condenser-water flow meter"). (a)
3. Data Feed 3: Compressor Input Power (ALREADY-RECORDED: stated in constraint "compressor input power"). (a)
4. Data Feed 4: Outdoor Wet-Bulb Temperature (ALREADY-RECORDED: standard BMS telemetry for open cooling towers; if absent, derived from local dry-bulb and RH BMS points).
5. Action Actuator: Existing Chemical Dosing Pump (a: Catalog part, AS-INSTALLED: Standard cooling tower dosing infrastructure already exists to maintain pH/conductivity; we utilize its existing flow-control capability, no new hardware installed).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Installability: Zero new hardware. Uses existing BMS points and existing dosing pumps.
Operability: Automated logic in BMS PLC. No operator intervention required for data collection.
Maintenance: None.
Operational Loss: 0. The indicator only triggers dosing when fouling exceeds baseline. Energy penalty of chemical dosing is negligible (<0.1% of chiller kWh).
Cost Class: Same as standard practice (no new sensors, no new pumps).
EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Retrieve 12-month historical BMS logs (ΔT_cond, T_wb, kW, Flow).
Calculation: Compute "Normalized Approach" = (T_cond_out - T_wb) * (kW_nominal / kW_actual) * (Flow_nominal / Flow_actual).
Baseline: Determine 95th percentile of historical Normalized Approach at low-load steady states to set the "Drift Threshold".
Pass/Fail: Simulate the 14-day pre-trip window. Does the Normalized Approach cross the Drift Threshold ≥14 days before the recorded Compressor Power reaches the high-head trip value?
Kill Criterion: If the signal-to-noise ratio of the Normalized Approach is <2:1 relative to ambient wet-bulb fluctuations, or if it does not lead the power trip by ≥14 days in historical data, the predictor fails.

CONSTRAINT BIND
Primary Stated Indicator: Compressor Input Power (threshold: high-head trip).
Reasoning: The failure is defined by "compressor power until a high-head trip." The indicator must predict when this power will reach the trip limit.
Permitted Set Compliance: Uses only listed signals (T_in, T_out, Flow, Power) + existing ambient telemetry. No new sensors. No refrigerant taps.
Mechanism Class: Dosing/Chemistry (permitted set: existing dosing system).
Deployment: No modification to chiller parts; utilizes surrounding water-system dosing infrastructure.
